All Trellix Enterprise (formerly McAfee Enterprise and FireEye) products, as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Trellix Advanced Research Center (Trellix ACR) that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Gridware software, services, and infrastructure issues, as well as vulnerabilities discovered by or reported to Gridware researchers that are not in another CNA’s scope.
Vulnerabilities discovered in Extreme Networks, Inc.’s products and services.
Juniper issues only.
All Rapid7 products, and vulnerabilities discovered by Rapid7 that are not in another CNA’s scope.

Vulnerabilities that are discovered, validated, and coordinated through the Hackrate Ethical Hacking Platform, including: software, web applications, APIs, and cloud services; vulnerabilities validated and triaged by our internal security team; and findings disclosed under our coordination that are not in another CNA’s scope.
All products of 2N Telekomunikace a.s. including end-of-life/end-of-service products.

Samsung TV & Appliance products, Samsung-owned open source projects listed on https://github.com/Samsung/, as well as vulnerabilities in third-party software discovered by Samsung that are not in another CNA’s scope. Vulnerabilities affecting end-of-life/end-of-service products are in scope. The following categories of Samsung Products are in scope: Internet-connected home appliances, B2C product (smart TV, smart monitor, soundbar, and projector), and B2B products (digital signage, interactive display, and kiosk).

items.organizationName: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Industrial Control Systems (ICS)
items.scope: Vulnerabilities that are (1) reported to or observed by CISA, (2) affect industrial control systems or medical devices, and (3) are not covered by another CNA’s scope.

Root Scope: Japan organizations.

All projects hosted by the Eclipse Foundation as listed at https://www.eclipse.org/projects/ and services provided by the Eclipse Foundation to support open source projects as listed at https://www.eclipsestatus.io/.

All Cisco products, and any third-party research targets that are not in another CNA’s scope. Cisco will not issue a CVE ID for issues reported on products that are past the Last Day of Support milestone, as defined on Cisco’s End-of-Life Policy, which is available at https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/eos-eol-policy.html.
SUSE and Rancher specific security issues, and vulnerabilities discovered by SUSE that are not covered by the scope of another CNA.
MongoDB products only, not including end-of-life components or products.
Core Joomla! CMS, the Joomla Framework, and Joomla! Extensions issues only.
All products and projects in which OpenVPN is directly involved commercially and for OpenVPN community projects, including Private Tunnel.
